lessons.title: White cross, white corners, middle layer

scenes.text: Nisha builds a white cross on top.
Each layer adds to the structure.

steps.title: Steps
steps.body:
1. **White cross** (intuitive): make a white plus on top with the side colours matching their centres.
2. **White corners:** turn the cube so the white face is down; bring a corner above its home and repeat **R U R' U'** until it drops in correctly.
3. **Middle layer:** for an edge going right: **U R U' R' U' F' U F**; for left: **U' L' U L U F U' F'**.

steps.title: Tips
steps.body: Hold the cube the same way, say moves aloud, and go slowly. If lost, reset: find the white cross again.

steps.title: Don't force the cube
steps.body: Never pry it apart; turn smoothly. Lubricate with silicone lubricant if it sticks.

steps.title: Yellow cross
steps.body: Use **F R U R' U' F'**. If you see only a dot, do it, then a line or L-shape appears; repeat until a yellow cross forms (hold a line horizontally; hold an L in the back-left).

steps.title: Permute the corners

lessons.title: Kitchen safety and food hygiene

scenes.text: Kiran, 18, moves into a shared flat in Coimbatore. On day two he smells gas when he enters the kitchen.
His flatmate reaches for the light switch. Kiran shouts ‘Stop!’ — he remembers his mother saying a spark can ignite gas.
They open windows, turn off the cylinder regulator and call the gas distributor’s emergency line.
Later that week, a flatmate gets food poisoning from rice left out overnight. The flat writes ‘kitchen rules’ on the fridge.

steps.title: WHO’s five keys to safer food
steps.body:
1. **Keep clean**: wash hands with soap before cooking and after touching raw meat, eggs, the bin or the toilet. Clean surfaces and cloths.
2. **Separate raw and cooked**: use different boards/knives for raw meat or fish; store raw meat below cooked food in the fridge.
3. **Cook thoroughly**: especially meat, poultry, eggs and seafood; reheat leftovers until steaming hot.
4. **Keep food at safe temperatures**: don’t leave cooked food at room temperature for more than about 2 hours; refrigerate promptly. Bacteria grow fastest roughly between 5 °C and 60 °C.
5. **Use safe water and raw materials**: wash fruits and vegetables; check dates.

steps.title: If you smell gas (LPG)
steps.body:
- **Do not** switch any electrical switch on or off, light a match or use a lighter.
- Open all doors and windows.
- Turn the cylinder **regulator OFF** and close the stove knobs.
- Leave the area and call the distributor or the LPG emergency helpline **1906** from outside.
- Don’t restart until checked. Replace cracked rubber tubes (they have an expiry date) and never keep the cylinder lying down.

steps.title: Pan fires and burns
steps.body:
If oil in a pan catches fire: **turn off the heat and cover the pan with a lid or a damp (not dripping) cloth**. **Never pour water** on burning oil — it explodes into a fireball. Don’t carry the burning pan. If it spreads, get out and call **112** or fire services **101**.

For small burns, cool under cool running water for about 20 minutes (see the first-aid course). Turn pan handles inward, away from children.

steps.title: Knife and kitchen habits
steps.body:
- Cut on a stable board (put a damp cloth under it so it doesn’t slip); curl fingertips in.
- A sharp knife is safer than a blunt one (less force, fewer slips).
- Never leave knives in a sink full of water.
- Wipe spills immediately to prevent falls.
- Keep a small fire blanket or extinguisher if possible, and know where it is.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Find your home’s gas regulator and practise turning it off. Check the date printed on the rubber tube. Write the LPG emergency number 1906 and your distributor’s number near the stove.

statements.s: If you smell gas, switch on the exhaust fan to clear it.
statements.why: Switching anything electrical can create a spark. Open windows instead.

statements.s: Pouring water on a burning oil pan is dangerous.
statements.why: Water turns to steam instantly and throws burning oil outward.

statements.s: Cooked rice left overnight at room temperature is always safe if reheated.
statements.why: Some bacteria make toxins that reheating doesn’t destroy. Refrigerate within about 2 hours.

statements.s: Raw chicken should be stored below cooked food in the fridge.
statements.why: So that drips from raw meat can’t contaminate ready-to-eat food.

statements.s: A blunt knife is safer than a sharp one.
statements.why: Blunt knives need more force and slip more easily.

quiz.q: First action when you enter a kitchen and smell gas?
options: Open windows and turn off the regulator without touching switches
quiz.why: With a gas smell, open windows and turn off the regulator without touching switches, as a spark could ignite the gas. Lighting a stove, switching on lights or an exhaust can cause an explosion.

quiz.q: A pan of oil catches fire. Best action?
options: Turn off heat and cover with a lid
quiz.why: For an oil fire, turn off the heat and cover the pan with a lid, which removes oxygen. Water makes burning oil flare up, and carrying the pan can spill it and burn you.

quiz.q: Cooked food should not stay at room temperature for more than about…
quiz.why: Cooked food should not stay at room temperature for more than about 2 hours because bacteria multiply quickly. Beyond that, it risks causing food poisoning.

quiz.q: Which is one of WHO’s five keys?
options: Wash meat in the sink near salad
Store raw meat on the top shelf
quiz.why: One of WHO's five keys to safer food is to separate raw and cooked food, which prevents cross-contamination. Washing meat near salad or tasting raw eggs spreads germs.

sources: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food
Oil marketing companies’ LPG safety guidance

lessons.title: Your first recipes: rice, dal, eggs and poha

scenes.text: Lena, an exchange student from Berlin, lives with Aditya’s family in Pune. She wants to learn ‘dal-chawal’.
Aditya admits he can’t cook either — his mother always did it.
His grandmother teaches both: wash, soak, measure water, count whistles, and finish with a tadka.
By the end of the week, both can make a full simple meal in 40 minutes.

steps.title: Rice (two ways)
steps.body:
**Measure**: about ½ cup (around 90–100 g) raw rice per adult per meal.
- **Absorption method (pot)**: wash rice 2–3 times until water is less cloudy. Use about **2 cups water per cup of rice** (varies by rice — basmati often a little less). Boil, lower heat, cover, cook ~15 minutes until water is absorbed, rest 5 minutes, fluff with a fork.
- **Pressure cooker**: rice + about 2 cups water per cup, 2 whistles on medium heat for many white rices, then let pressure drop naturally.
Common mistake: stirring often (makes it mushy) or too much water.

steps.title: Simple dal tadka
steps.body:
1. Wash ½ cup toor (arhar) dal; soak 20 minutes if time allows.
2. Pressure cook with about 1½ cups water, a pinch of turmeric and salt, ~3–4 whistles, until soft.
3. Release pressure fully before opening. Mash lightly; add water for the thickness you like.
4. **Tadka**: heat 1–2 tsp oil or ghee, add cumin (jeera) seeds; when they sizzle add chopped garlic/onion, then tomato, a pinch of chilli powder. Pour over dal.
5. Add lemon or coriander. Taste and adjust salt.

steps.title: Pressure cooker safety
steps.body:
- Don’t fill beyond about **two-thirds** (about **half** for dal, beans and rice that foam).
- Check that the gasket (rubber ring) and vent are clean before each use.
- **Never force the lid open**. Let pressure release naturally or as the manual says.
- If the safety valve hisses or leaks repeatedly, stop and get it checked.
- Keep the cooker off when you step away for long.

steps.title: Two 10-minute dishes
steps.body:
**Omelette**: beat 2 eggs with salt, chopped onion, chilli and coriander. Heat a little oil on medium, pour, let set, fold. Cook until no liquid egg remains.

**Poha**: rinse thick poha in a strainer (don’t soak long), add a little salt and turmeric. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, peanuts, onion; then potato cubes if using (cook till soft); add poha, mix gently, cover 2 minutes; finish with lemon and coriander.

steps.title: Cook like a pro
steps.body:
- **Mise en place**: chop and measure everything before you light the stove.
- **Taste as you go**; salt can be added, not removed.
- **Clean as you go** so the kitchen isn’t a disaster at the end.
- Cook a bigger batch of dal and refrigerate in a covered box for up to a day or two.

activity.prompt: Put the dal tadka steps in order.
items: Wash the dal
Pressure cook with water, turmeric and salt
Let pressure release fully, then open
Heat oil or ghee and add cumin seeds
Add garlic, onion and tomato
Pour the tadka over the dal and serve

quiz.q: About how much water for 1 cup of white rice using the absorption method?
quiz.why: About 2 cups of water per 1 cup of white rice is a common ratio for the absorption method; adjust by rice type. Half a cup is too little and 6 cups is far too much.

quiz.q: How full should a pressure cooker be for dal?
quiz.why: Fill a pressure cooker only about half for dal, because foaming foods need space or they can block the vent. Filling it to the brim is unsafe.

options: Spices tempered in hot oil or ghee poured over a dish
quiz.why: A tadka is spices tempered in hot oil or ghee and poured over a dish, which releases their flavour into the fat. It is not a salad, rice type or pot.

quiz.q: Before opening a pressure cooker you must…
options: Pour cold water on the lid while it whistles
quiz.why: Let the pressure release fully before opening a cooker, because opening it under pressure can cause severe burns. Forcing the lid or pouring cold water on it is dangerous.

lessons.title: Meal planning, groceries and reading food labels

scenes.text: Newly married Pooja and Sameer in Indore spend a lot on groceries and food delivery, yet half the vegetables rot.
They try a challenge: plan seven days of meals, shop once with a list, and buy fresh vegetables twice a week.
They store food correctly and cook leftovers into new dishes.
At the end of the month they spent much less and threw almost nothing away.

steps.title: Plan in 15 minutes a week
steps.body:
1. Check what you already have (fridge, shelves).
2. Plan breakfasts, lunches and dinners for 7 days; reuse ingredients across meals (e.g., one bunch of spinach → dal palak + paratha).
3. Write a list grouped by section: grains & pulses, vegetables, fruit, dairy, protein, spices, cleaning.
4. Shop once a week for staples and once or twice for fresh produce.
5. Keep one ‘flex’ night for leftovers or eating out.

steps.title: Reading Indian food labels
steps.body:
Packaged food labels must show the product name, ingredients, nutrition information, net quantity, MRP, date of manufacture/packing, best before or use by date, and the **FSSAI logo with licence number**. A **green mark** in a square means vegetarian; a **brown mark** means non-vegetarian.
- **Use by**: about safety — don’t eat after it.
- **Best before**: about quality — may still be safe if stored well, but quality falls.
Ingredients are listed in descending order by weight: if sugar is first or second, it’s a sugary product.

steps.title: Storage that prevents waste
steps.body:
- Leafy greens: wrap in a dry cloth or paper in the fridge.
- Onions and potatoes: cool, dry, dark place, **not together** (they spoil each other faster).
- Tomatoes and bananas ripen others — keep apart if you want slower ripening.
- Store grains and pulses in airtight jars; add a date label.
- **First in, first out**: move older items to the front.

steps.title: Leftover magic
steps.body:
- Leftover rice → lemon rice or curd rice (only if refrigerated properly).
- Leftover dal → dal paratha or thicker dal with fresh tadka.
- Leftover sabzi → wraps/frankie with roti.
- Overripe bananas → banana pancakes or shake.
Cool leftovers quickly, cover, refrigerate, and eat within a day or two.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Write a 7-day menu for your home and a grocery list from it. Then play the **Market Day** game to practise buying within a budget.

activity.prompt: Where should each item be stored?

quiz.why: 'Use by' is mainly about safety, so do not eat food after that date. 'Best before' is about quality.

quiz.q: On an Indian food pack, a green mark in a square means…
quiz.why: A green mark in a square on an Indian food pack means vegetarian; a brown mark means non-vegetarian. It does not mean sugar-free, organic or imported.

quiz.q: If sugar is the first ingredient listed, the product…
options: Has the most sugar by weight
quiz.why: Ingredients are listed in descending order by weight, so if sugar is first the product has more sugar than any other ingredient. It is not sugar-free.

quiz.q: Which habit most reduces food waste?
options: Buying the biggest pack of everything
Planning meals and using first in, first out
quiz.why: Planning meals and using first in, first out prevents spoilage and waste. Shopping without a list or buying the biggest packs leads to throwing food away.

lessons.title: A balanced plate on a budget

scenes.text: Mr. D’Souza, 66, in Goa, eats mostly white rice with a little curry. His doctor says he needs more protein and vegetables.
His granddaughter Tanya draws his plate as a pie: half vegetables and fruit, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.
They add affordable proteins: chana, rajma, eggs, fish, curd, peanuts.
Three months later he says he feels stronger walking to church.

steps.title: The half–quarter–quarter plate
steps.body:
A simple visual guide used by many health bodies:
- **Half the plate**: vegetables (and some fruit through the day) — different colours.
- **A quarter**: whole grains or millets (brown rice, whole-wheat roti, jowar, bajra, ragi).
- **A quarter**: protein (dal, beans, chana, eggs, fish, chicken, paneer, tofu, curd).
- Plus a little healthy fat (oil, nuts, seeds) and water.
India’s National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN) publishes dietary guidelines with a similar balanced-plate idea.

steps.title: Cheap protein swaps
steps.body:
- Mix dal + rice or roti: grains and pulses together give a better protein mix.
- **Chana, rajma, moong, lobia**: buy dry, soak overnight, pressure cook — much cheaper than canned.
- **Sprouts**: soak moong for 8 hours, drain, keep covered 1–2 days; rinse daily.
- **Eggs**, **curd** and **peanuts** are affordable protein sources.
- **Seasonal vegetables** are cheaper and fresher than off-season ones.

steps.title: Common food mistakes
steps.body:
- Too much salt (pickles, papad, packaged snacks) — linked to high blood pressure.
- Sugary drinks counted as ‘just a drink’.
- Skipping breakfast then overeating at night.
- Deep-frying in reused oil repeatedly.
This is general education. People with diabetes, kidney disease, allergies, pregnancy or other conditions should follow advice from a doctor or registered dietitian.

steps.title: Small, lasting changes
steps.body: Change one thing a week: add a vegetable to breakfast; swap one white-rice meal for millet; keep roasted chana for snacks; drink water before reaching for a soft drink. Habits beat strict diets.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Photograph your next lunch. Is half the plate vegetables? Is there a protein? Plan one change for tomorrow.

activity.prompt: Match the food to its main role on the plate.

quiz.q: On a balanced plate, vegetables and fruit should be about…
quiz.why: A common guide for a balanced plate is about half vegetables and fruit, with the rest grains and protein. A tiny corner or the whole plate is unbalanced.
Chana (chickpeas) is an affordable vegetarian protein; pulses are protein-rich and cheap. Sugar, soft drinks and chips give little protein.

quiz.q: Why combine dal with rice or roti?
options: Grains and pulses complement each other’s proteins
quiz.why: Grains and pulses complement each other's proteins, so together they provide a better range of amino acids. It is nutrition, not just taste.

quiz.q: Who should get personalised diet advice from a professional?
options: People with conditions like diabetes or kidney disease
quiz.why: People with conditions like diabetes or kidney disease need individual guidance because the wrong diet can harm them. General advice may not fit their medical needs.

questions.why: Wash your hands with soap before cooking, because clean hands prevent contamination of food. Tasting raw meat or leaving burners on is unsafe.

questions.q: The LPG emergency helpline number in India is…
questions.why: The LPG emergency helpline in India is 1906. 14416 is mental health, 1098 is Childline and 1930 is cyber fraud.

questions.q: Which is a whole grain or millet?
questions.why: Ragi (finger millet) is a whole grain millet. Maida biscuits are refined, and sugar and soft drinks are not grains.

questions.q: Burning oil in a pan — never use…
questions.why: Never use water on burning oil; it sinks, turns to steam and causes an explosive flare-up. Turning off the heat, using a lid or a damp cloth is safe.
Raw meat should be stored below cooked food so its drips cannot fall on ready-to-eat items. Above or next to salad risks contamination.
'Best before' means the food has best quality until that date; it is a quality indicator, not a safety date like 'use by'. It is not the manufacture date.

questions.q: For a pressure cooker, the gasket should be…
questions.why: A pressure cooker gasket should be clean and in good condition, because a faulty one causes leaks and pressure problems. Never ignore or remove it.

questions.q: Ingredients: ‘sugar, wheat flour, palm oil…’. This product is…
questions.why: Ingredients are listed by weight, largest first, so a list starting with sugar means the product is mostly sugar by weight. It cannot be sugar-free or high protein.

questions.q: Why shouldn’t onions and potatoes be stored together?
questions.why: Onions and potatoes should be stored apart because moisture and gases from each speed up the other's spoilage.

questions.q: You cooked a big pot of rice at 1 pm. Safest plan for leftovers?
options: Freeze after 2 days at room temperature
Keep in a warm oven overnight
Cool and refrigerate within about 2 hours, reheat till steaming, eat within a day
questions.why: Cool and refrigerate rice within about 2 hours, reheat till steaming and eat within a day. Leaving rice out lets bacteria grow and produce toxins that reheating may not remove.

questions.q: Which weekly plan reduces cost AND waste most?
options: Buying all vegetables for a month
Menu → list → one staples trip + 1–2 fresh trips, reuse ingredients
questions.why: A menu, list, one staples trip and 1–2 fresh trips with reused ingredients match buying to use, cutting cost and waste. Bulk monthly vegetables spoil and random shopping or ordering costs more.

questions.q: A gas smell at night: correct sequence?
options: Don’t touch switches → open windows → regulator off → leave → call 1906/distributor from outside
questions.why: Do not touch switches, open windows, turn the regulator off, leave, then call 1906 or the distributor from outside. This avoids sparks, ventilates, isolates the gas and gets experts. Fans, candles and lights can ignite it.

questions.q: A family wants more protein without big cost. Best combined advice?
options: Add pulses/sprouts, eggs or curd daily, pair grains with dal, buy seasonal vegetables
questions.why: Add pulses or sprouts, eggs or curd daily, pair grains with dal and buy seasonal vegetables to raise protein cheaply within a balanced plate. Cutting vegetables, skipping meals or powder alone is not better.

courses.title: Cleaning, laundry, small repairs & waste
courses.summary: A cleaning routine that actually works, laundry without ruining clothes, safe small repairs (MCB, taps, drains), and segregating waste the right way.
outcomes: Learners can plan a daily/weekly/monthly cleaning routine
Learners know which cleaning chemicals must never be mixed

lessons.title: A cleaning routine that doesn’t take all weekend

story.title: The flat that never felt clean

scenes.text: Three flatmates in Noida — Ayesha, Neha and Ben from Canada — clean only when guests come. Every Sunday becomes a fight.
Ayesha makes a chart: 10 minutes daily each, one weekly zone each, monthly deep tasks rotating.
Ben once mixed bleach with a toilet cleaner and started coughing. They learn chemical safety the hard way.
Within a month the flat stays tidy and Sundays are free again.

steps.title: Two principles: top to bottom, dry to wet
steps.body: Dust falls down, so clean **high surfaces first** (fans, shelves) and floors **last**. Do **dry work first** (dusting, sweeping) and **wet work after** (wiping, mopping) — otherwise you turn dust into mud. Work from the far end of a room towards the door so you don’t walk on wet floors.

steps.title: A simple routine
steps.body:
**Daily (10–15 minutes)**: wash dishes, wipe kitchen counter and stove, sweep main areas, empty bins, put things back.
**Weekly**: mop floors, clean bathroom and toilet, change bed sheets, dust furniture, wipe fridge shelves, clean mirrors.
**Monthly**: fan blades, windows and grills, kitchen tiles and chimney filter, under furniture, throw out expired items.
Split by person or by day — fairness matters more than perfection.

steps.title: Never mix these
steps.body:
- **Bleach + acid-based cleaners** (many toilet cleaners, vinegar) → releases **chlorine gas**.
- **Bleach + ammonia** (some glass cleaners) → toxic **chloramine** gas.
- Don’t mix different drain cleaners.
Use one product at a time, rinse between, keep windows open, wear gloves, keep chemicals in original labelled bottles, out of children’s reach. If someone feels breathless after fumes, move them to fresh air and seek medical help.

steps.title: Cheap, effective basics
steps.body:
- Soap/detergent and water clean most things.
- Microfibre cloths trap dust better than old rags.
- Colour-code cloths: one for kitchen, a different one for bathroom.
- Wash and dry cloths and mops often — a damp smelly mop spreads germs.
- ‘One in, one out’: when something new comes in, something old goes out — less clutter, less cleaning.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Set a 10-minute timer and do the daily list now. Then write a weekly chart for your home with names against each task.

activity.prompt: How often should each task usually be done?

quiz.q: Which should you clean first in a room?
quiz.why: Clean top to bottom, starting with the ceiling fan and high shelves, because dust falls down onto surfaces below. Cleaning the floor first means redoing it.

quiz.q: Mixing bleach with an acidic toilet cleaner can release…
quiz.why: Bleach mixed with an acidic toilet cleaner can release toxic chlorine gas. This is a dangerous and common household accident, so never mix cleaners.

quiz.q: Why do dry tasks before wet ones?
options: Wet first turns dust into mud
Brooms work better on wet floors
quiz.why: Do dry tasks like sweeping and dusting before wet ones, because wetting dust first turns it into mud. Then wipe or mop.

quiz.q: Using the same cloth for toilet and kitchen…
quiz.why: Using the same cloth for toilet and kitchen spreads germs to food areas. Colour-code cloths to avoid cross-contamination.

sources: Poison-control and household chemical safety guidance

lessons.title: Laundry: labels, sorting and stains

scenes.text: Rohit, 19, washes his new red kurta with all his white school shirts in Ranchi.
Everything comes out pink. His favourite wool sweater, washed in hot water, has shrunk to a child’s size.
His neighbour Aunty Mary, who runs a tailoring shop, shows him the small care label inside every garment.
Now he sorts, reads labels and treats stains early. No more pink shirts.

steps.title: Read the care label
steps.body:
Care labels use symbols:
- **Tub with water**: washing; a number (30, 40, 60) is the maximum temperature in °C; a hand in the tub = hand wash; a cross = do not wash.
- **Triangle**: bleach (crossed out = no bleach).
- **Square with a circle**: tumble dry (dots = heat level).
- **Iron**: dots show heat (1 low, 3 high).
- **Circle**: dry clean only.
When in doubt: cold or lukewarm water, gentle cycle, dry in shade.

steps.title: Sorting and washing
steps.body:
1. **Sort** into whites/lights, darks/colours, delicates, and heavy items (towels, jeans).
2. **Test new coloured clothes** for colour bleeding: dab a wet white cloth on a hidden part; if colour transfers, wash separately.
3. Empty pockets (tissues, pens, coins).
4. Turn dark and printed clothes inside out to reduce fading.
5. Don’t overload the machine — clothes need room to move.
6. Use the detergent amount on the pack; more is **not** cleaner (leaves residue).

steps.title: Stain first aid
steps.body:
Act fast, **blot, don’t rub** (rubbing spreads and pushes the stain in).
- **Blood**: rinse in **cold** water (hot water sets it), then detergent.
- **Oil/grease**: sprinkle talc or apply a little dish-washing liquid, let sit, then wash.
- **Tea/coffee**: rinse quickly with cold water from the back of the stain, then wash.
- **Turmeric (haldi)**: wash with soap and dry in sunlight — sun often fades the yellow.
- **Ink**: test any remover on a hidden spot first.
Always check the stain is gone **before** drying with heat or ironing; heat makes stains permanent.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Hot water on wool or silk (shrinkage, damage).
- Leaving wet clothes in the machine for hours (smell, mould).
- Drying dark clothes in harsh sun for long (fading).
- Bleaching coloured clothes.
- Ironing on the highest heat for synthetic fabric (melting).

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Pick five clothes from your cupboard and read their labels. Sort them into wash groups. Write down which needs cold water or hand wash.

activity.prompt: Match the stain or problem to the right first step.
pairs: Talc or dish-washing liquid, then wash
Soap wash and dry in sunlight
Test for colour bleeding; wash separately
Cold water, gentle or hand wash, dry flat
Clothes forgotten wet in the machine

quiz.why: The number in the wash tub symbol is the maximum wash temperature, so 30 means a maximum of 30 °C. It is not minutes or number of clothes.

quiz.q: Blood stains should be rinsed in…
quiz.why: Rinse blood stains in cold water, because hot water sets protein stains so they are hard to remove. Oil or tea will not help.

options: Can leave residue and irritate skin
quiz.why: Using double detergent does not clean better; excess detergent does not rinse out well and can leave residue that irritates skin. It does not waterproof clothes.

quiz.q: Why blot instead of rubbing a stain?
options: Rubbing spreads it and pushes it deeper
quiz.why: Rubbing a stain spreads it and pushes it deeper into the fibres, while blotting lifts it without spreading it.

lessons.title: Small repairs you can do safely

scenes.text: Every time Mrs. Banerjee in Durgapur switches on her new electric kettle with the microwave, the lights go off.
She used to call an electrician each time and pay a visit fee.
Her son Arnav learns how the MCB board works, why it trips, and when it is a sign of real danger.
He also fixes a dripping tap and a slow drain — and knows when to stop and call a professional.

steps.title: A basic home toolkit
steps.body: Screwdrivers (flat and Phillips), a **tester screwdriver** (line tester), pliers, adjustable spanner, measuring tape, torch, insulating tape, plumber’s (PTFE/Teflon) tape, a plunger, spare tap washers, a few screws and wall plugs, super glue, and gloves. Keep them in one box that everyone knows.

steps.title: When the MCB trips
steps.body:
An **MCB** (miniature circuit breaker) switches off a circuit when too much current flows (overload or short circuit). An **RCCB/RCD** trips if current leaks, for example through a person — it protects against electric shock.
1. Switch off and unplug appliances on that circuit.
2. Push the MCB lever back up (ON).
3. Plug in appliances one by one. If one makes it trip, that appliance is faulty or you are overloading.
4. If it trips **immediately with nothing plugged in**, or you smell burning, see sparks or the switchboard is hot — **stop and call a licensed electrician**.

steps.title: Electrical safety rules
steps.body:
- Never work on wiring with wet hands or standing on a wet floor.
- Switch off the **main** before changing a switch, fitting or fan.
- Never replace an MCB with a bigger rating ‘to stop tripping’ or bypass an RCCB.
- Don’t overload a single socket with many adapters.
- If someone gets an electric shock: **don’t touch them** until power is off; switch off the main or move the source with a dry non-conducting object; then call **112** and give first aid.

steps.title: Dripping tap and slow drain
steps.body:
**Dripping tap** (screw-type): close the angle valve or the main water valve, open the tap to drain, unscrew the head, replace the worn rubber washer with the same size, reassemble with PTFE tape on threads where needed. Ceramic/quarter-turn taps use a cartridge instead.

**Slow drain**: remove hair and gunk from the grating; use a **plunger** (cover the overflow hole, plunge firmly 10–15 times); pour hot (not boiling, for plastic pipes) water. Avoid mixing chemical drain cleaners; never use them along with plunging. Prevent clogs with a mesh strainer and by never pouring cooking oil down the sink.

steps.title: Know when to call a pro
steps.body: Call a licensed professional for: new wiring, repeated tripping, burning smells, water leaking inside walls, gas lines, anything on a ladder you’re unsure about, and tall-building work. A good rule: if a mistake could cause a fire, flood, shock or fall, get help.

a.text: The kitchen lights go off when you switch on the kettle. The MCB board shows one lever down. What first?

choices.label: Unplug the kettle and other kitchen appliances, then switch the MCB back on
choices.feedback: Right — remove the load before resetting.

choices.label: Tape the lever up so it can’t trip again
choices.feedback: Never defeat a safety device. It can cause a fire.

b.text: The MCB stays on. You plug in the kettle alone and it trips again immediately.

choices.label: Stop using the kettle; get it checked or replaced
choices.feedback: The kettle is likely faulty (short or leakage).

choices.label: Open the kettle base with wet hands to look inside
choices.feedback: Wet hands + electrical device = shock risk.

bad.text: Dangerous choice. Safety devices trip for a reason. Switch off the main, and call a licensed electrician.

good.text: Well done — you found the faulty appliance safely and the home stays protected.

options: Cuts power when a circuit is overloaded or shorted
quiz.why: An MCB (miniature circuit breaker) cuts power when a circuit is overloaded or shorted, protecting wiring. It does not store electricity or brighten lights.

quiz.q: Before replacing a tap washer you must…
quiz.why: Close the water valve before replacing a tap washer, otherwise water gushes out when you open the tap.

quiz.q: Someone is stuck to a live wire. First step?
options: Switch off power or push the source away with a dry non-conducting object
quiz.why: Switch off the power or push the source away with a dry non-conducting object. Touching the person with bare hands or using water can shock you too.

quiz.q: Which should you never pour down a kitchen sink?
quiz.why: Never pour cooking oil down the sink; it solidifies and clogs the pipes. Water, soapy water and rinse water are fine.

quiz.q: MCB trips even with nothing plugged in. You should…
quiz.why: An MCB that trips with nothing plugged in may mean a wiring fault, which is a fire risk, so call a licensed electrician. A bigger MCB or repeated resets hides the danger.

sources: Bureau of Indian Standards / Central Electricity Authority safety guidance

lessons.title: Waste segregation, composting and pests

scenes.text: In a housing society in Mysuru, all waste goes in one bag. The collection van often refuses it, and stray animals tear bags open.
Resident Mrs. Gowda starts a two-bin drive: green for wet, blue for dry, plus a box for hazardous items.
Wet waste becomes compost for the society garden. Dry waste goes to a recycler.
They also clear stagnant water from pots and coolers — dengue cases in the building drop.

steps.title: Three streams (as per India’s Solid Waste Management Rules 2016)
steps.body:
Households should segregate waste into:
- **Wet / biodegradable**: vegetable and fruit peels, leftover food, tea leaves, eggshells, garden leaves.
- **Dry / non-biodegradable**: plastic, paper, cardboard, metal, glass, cloth, packaging (keep it clean and dry so it can be recycled).
- **Domestic hazardous**: batteries, expired medicines, paint cans, chemical containers, broken CFL/tubelights, used needles.
Sanitary waste (diapers, pads) should be wrapped securely in paper/newspaper and handed over as per local instructions. E-waste (old phones, chargers) goes to authorised e-waste collectors.

steps.title: Composting at home
steps.body:
A simple pot or bucket method:
1. Drill small holes in a bucket or use a terracotta compost pot.
2. Layer **greens** (wet kitchen waste) with **browns** (dry leaves, shredded paper, cocopeat) roughly 1:1 or more browns.
3. Keep it moist like a squeezed sponge; mix every few days.
4. No meat, dairy or oil in simple home bins (smell, pests).
5. In about 6–8 weeks you get dark, earthy compost.
Smelly? Add more browns. Too dry? Sprinkle water.

steps.title: Mosquitoes, rats and cockroaches
steps.body:
- **Aedes mosquitoes** (dengue, chikungunya) breed in **clean stagnant water** and bite mostly in the **daytime**. Empty water from flower-pot trays, coolers, tyres, buckets and water tanks at least **once a week**; cover tanks.
- Keep food covered; take out wet waste daily.
- Seal gaps around pipes; fix leaks (cockroaches love moisture).
- Use pesticides only as labelled, away from food and children; store them locked.

steps.title: Reduce before recycle
steps.body: Carry a cloth bag, a water bottle and a lunch box. Refuse what you don’t need, reuse what you can, repair before replacing, then recycle. The cleanest waste is the waste never created.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Label two bins at home (wet/dry) and one small box for hazardous items. Walk around your home and empty any standing water.

activity.prompt: Sort the waste into the right stream.

quiz.why: Used batteries are domestic hazardous waste because they contain chemicals and metals that harm the environment. Peels, newspaper and a steel spoon are not hazardous.
Aedes mosquitoes that spread dengue breed in clean stagnant water collected in containers. They do not breed in dry sand or fast running rivers.
Keep dry waste clean so it can be recycled, because food-soiled packaging often cannot be recycled.

quiz.q: Compost smells bad. Most likely fix?
options: Add more browns like dry leaves
quiz.why: A smelly compost usually has too much wet material, so add more 'browns' like dry leaves to balance it. Meat and oil worsen smell and sealing it airtight does too.

sources: National Centre for Vector Borne Diseases Control — dengue prevention

questions.q: Clean a room in which order?
questions.why: Clean a room from top to bottom, because dust falls downward and would dirty a floor already cleaned.
Banana peels are biodegradable, so they go in wet waste, not e-waste, dry or hazardous waste.

questions.q: Which tool clears a blocked sink without chemicals?
questions.why: A plunger clears a blocked sink without chemicals by using pressure to dislodge the clog. An iron, hammer or ladder cannot.
Never mix bleach with acidic toilet cleaner or ammonia, because toxic gases form. Mixing it with water is normal dilution.

questions.q: A cross over a triangle on a label means…
questions.why: A triangle on a care label is the bleach symbol, and a cross over it means do not bleach. No ironing and dry cleaning have different symbols.
Aedes mosquitoes, the dengue vectors, mostly bite during the day, so protection is needed in daytime too.

questions.q: Which device protects people against electric shock from leakage current?
questions.why: An RCCB/RCD detects leakage current to earth and cuts power to protect people from electric shock. An MCB protects against overload and short circuit, not leakage.

questions.q: Blood on a white shirt: what NOT to do?
questions.why: Do not wash blood in hot water first; hot water sets the stain. Blot, rinse in cold water and use detergent.

options: Put in domestic hazardous waste / take-back as per local rules
questions.why: Expired medicines are hazardous waste, so put them in domestic hazardous waste or a take-back scheme per local rules. Do not flush, burn or give them to pets.

questions.q: MCB trips repeatedly with one specific iron plugged in. Most likely?
options: The iron is faulty or draws too much for that circuit
MCB too small, replace with bigger
questions.why: If the MCB trips only with one iron plugged in, that iron is faulty or draws too much for that circuit. Isolating appliances finds the fault; never replace the MCB with a bigger one.

questions.q: Flatmates keep arguing about cleaning. Most effective fix?
options: A written daily/weekly/monthly rota shared fairly
questions.why: A written, fairly shared daily, weekly and monthly rota makes duties clear and visible, so it reduces arguments. One person doing everything or cleaning only for guests causes conflict.

questions.q: A family member is dizzy after cleaning a bathroom with two products. Correct response?
options: Move to fresh air, ventilate, stop using the products, seek medical help if symptoms persist or are severe (call 112)
questions.why: Move the person to fresh air, ventilate, stop using the products and get medical help if symptoms persist or are severe (call 112). Mixed cleaners may release toxic fumes; air freshener or continuing makes it worse.

questions.q: Which combination best prevents dengue at home?
options: Weekly emptying of containers, covering tanks, using nets/repellents in the daytime
questions.why: Weekly emptying of containers, covering tanks and using nets or repellents in the daytime remove breeding sites and prevent bites. Removing breeding sites weekly is the key; fogging once a year or full coolers do not control dengue.

courses.title: Renting a flat: search, agreement, living, moving out
courses.summary: How to find a flat without being scammed, what a rent agreement must contain, registration and stamp duty basics, tenant verification, and how to get your deposit back.
outcomes: Learners can set a rent budget and inspect a flat with a checklist
Learners can list the essential clauses of a rent agreement
Learners can explain why many agreements are 11 months and what registration means
Learners can document a flat’s condition at move-in
Learners can handle deposit disputes calmly and in writing

lessons.title: Finding a flat (and avoiding rental scams)

scenes.text: Sneha, 23, moves to Hyderabad for her first job. She finds a beautiful 1BHK online at a surprisingly low rent.
The ‘owner’ says he is abroad and asks for ₹15,000 ‘token advance’ on UPI before she can see the flat.
Her colleague Farhan says: never pay before you see the flat and meet the owner. They check — the photos are copied from another listing.
She finds a real flat through a verified visit, with a checklist, and negotiates the rent.

steps.title: Set your budget first
steps.body:
A common guideline: keep rent around **25–30% of take-home pay** (it may be higher in expensive cities, then cut elsewhere). Add the hidden costs:
- Security deposit (often 2–3 months in many cities; in some cities more)
- Brokerage (often around one month’s rent if you use a broker; negotiate)
- Maintenance charges, electricity, water, internet, gas, furniture
- Moving costs and the first month’s rent.

steps.title: The visit checklist
steps.body:
- **Water**: pressure, timing, hard/soft water, any tanker dependence.
- **Walls/ceiling**: seepage, damp patches, cracks (check corners and under sinks).
- **Electricity**: number of sockets, earthing, meter type, power backup.
- **Light and air**: does sunlight reach? Cross-ventilation?
- **Mobile network** inside the flat.
- **Safety**: door locks, grills, guard, CCTV, fire exits, lighting in the lane at night.
- **Distance**: commute time at peak hours; hospital, market.
- **Rules**: society rules about guests, pets, food, bachelors, parking.

steps.title: Rental scam red flags
steps.body:
- Rent far below the area’s typical rent.
- ‘I’m abroad / in the army, pay token and I’ll courier keys.’
- Pressure: ‘three people want it, pay in one hour.’
- No visit allowed; owner won’t video-call from the flat.
- Documents that don’t match (name on electricity bill vs owner).
Never pay before visiting and seeing ownership proof (e.g., property tax receipt or sale deed copy plus ID). Pay deposits by bank transfer to the owner’s account with a written receipt.

steps.title: Negotiating
steps.body: Ask politely for: lower deposit, fixing issues before move-in (written), a smaller yearly increase, inclusion of existing furniture, or a waived painting charge. Visiting several flats gives you a fair sense of the market and confidence to negotiate.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Compute your maximum rent (30% of take-home) and the total cash needed to move in (deposit + brokerage + first rent + moving).

activity.prompt: Flat visit checklist — tick when checked
items: Turned on taps and checked water pressure
Looked for damp patches and seepage
Tested a few sockets and switches
Checked mobile signal inside
Checked door lock and window grills
Walked the lane after dark
Asked about society rules
Saw owner ID and proof of ownership
Asked total maintenance and utility costs

quiz.q: A common guideline for rent is…
quiz.why: A common guideline is that rent should be around 25–30% of take-home pay, leaving room for other needs and savings. 80% would leave too little for living costs.

quiz.q: An ‘owner’ abroad asks for token money before any visit. This is…
quiz.why: An 'owner' abroad who asks for token money before any visit is a common rental scam. Never pay before seeing the property and getting proof of ownership.

quiz.q: Best way to pay a security deposit?
options: Bank transfer to the owner’s account with written receipt
quiz.why: Pay a deposit by bank transfer to the owner's account with a written receipt, which creates proof. Cash without receipt, crypto or gift cards leave no reliable record.
Damp patches on walls suggest seepage or leakage, which can mean mould and health problems. They are not a sign of good ventilation.

sources: Consumer awareness on rental fraud (police cyber cell advisories)

lessons.title: The rent agreement: what it must say

scenes.text: Joseph in Chennai signs a one-page agreement without reading. When he leaves, the landlord keeps his whole deposit for ‘painting and cleaning’.
His friend Meenakshi’s agreement lists the deposit, refund timeline, notice period and a move-in inventory with photos.
When she leaves, deductions are limited to a broken fan regulator, as agreed.
Joseph learns: the agreement is your protection — read and negotiate before signing.

steps.title: Essential clauses
steps.body:
- Names and addresses of landlord and tenant(s); property address.
- **Rent** amount, due date, payment mode; late-payment terms.
- **Security deposit** amount and **refund timeline and conditions**.
- **Term** (start and end date), **renewal** and **yearly increase** (e.g., 5%).
- **Lock-in period** (if any) and **notice period** for both sides.
- Who pays **maintenance, electricity, water, property tax**.
- **Repairs**: which are tenant’s (minor) and landlord’s (structural, major).
- Use (residential only), subletting rules, guests/pets if relevant.
- **Inventory** of fixtures and furniture (annexure).

steps.title: Why many agreements are 11 months
steps.body: Under the **Registration Act 1908**, a lease of immovable property for **one year or more** must be registered. Many people therefore use **11-month** agreements on stamp paper (or e-stamp), which are often not registered, to avoid registration fees and procedures. However, **stamp duty** rules and registration practices vary by state, and some states (for example, Maharashtra) require registration of leave-and-licence agreements regardless of period. A registered agreement is stronger evidence in a dispute. Check your state’s rules — many states offer online e-registration.

steps.title: The Model Tenancy Act 2021
steps.body: The central government released a **Model Tenancy Act** in 2021 as a template for states. It applies only where a state adopts its own law based on it. It proposes written agreements reported to a Rent Authority, a cap on residential security deposits (two months’ rent), clear repair duties and a faster dispute process. Old **Rent Control Acts** still apply in many states. So rules depend on where you live.

steps.title: Read before you sign
steps.body:
- Blank spaces → fill or strike out.
- Vague clause: ‘deductions as per owner’s discretion’ → ask for specific terms.
- Very long lock-in (you pay penalty if you leave early).
- Clauses allowing entry anytime without notice.
- Keep a signed copy with all pages initialled; both parties and two witnesses usually sign.

steps.title: General education
steps.body: This is general education, not legal advice. Laws and stamp duty differ by state and change over time; for high-value or unusual arrangements, consult a lawyer or your state’s registration department.

statements.s: In India, a lease of one year or more generally must be registered under the Registration Act.
The Model Tenancy Act 2021 automatically applies in every state.
statements.why: It is a model; states must adopt their own law.

statements.s: An agreement should state the security deposit and how and when it will be refunded.
Stamp duty on rent agreements is the same in every state.
statements.why: Stamp duty is set by each state.

statements.s: Initialling every page and keeping a signed copy is a good habit.
statements.why: Prevents page substitution and gives you proof.

quiz.q: Why are many rent agreements for 11 months?
options: Leases of one year or more generally need registration
quiz.why: Leases of one year or more generally need to be registered, which costs time and money, so many agreements are for 11 months. It is a legal and cost reason, not tradition.

quiz.q: A notice period clause tells you…
options: How early either side must inform before ending the agreement
quiz.why: A notice period clause says how early either side must inform the other before ending the agreement. It is not about Wi-Fi, rent due dates or police details.

quiz.q: The Model Tenancy Act proposes a residential deposit cap of…
quiz.why: The Model Tenancy Act proposes a residential security deposit cap of two months' rent, where a state adopts it. It is not ten months or a full year.
'Deductions at owner's discretion' is vague and invites disputes, so negotiate specific terms for what can be deducted. It is neither clear nor required by law.

sources: Model Tenancy Act 2021 (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs)

lessons.title: Moving in: inventory, verification and rent receipts

scenes.text: On move-in day in Bengaluru, Ishaan records a slow video of every room, the scratched kitchen counter and a cracked bathroom tile.
He emails it to his landlord with the date and meter readings.
The landlord reminds him to complete police tenant verification, which the city requires.
Two years later, the landlord tries to charge for the cracked tile. Ishaan forwards the old email. Problem solved.

steps.title: Move-in documentation
steps.body:
1. **Inventory list**: every fan, light, geyser, AC, furniture item, curtain rod, key — with condition.
2. **Dated photos/video** of every wall, floor, fixture and existing damage.
3. **Meter readings**: electricity, water, gas.
4. Email or message all of it to the landlord the same day and ask for acknowledgement.
5. Count and label keys.

steps.title: Police tenant verification
steps.body: Many Indian cities and states require landlords to get **tenant verification** done with the local police; it is usually the landlord’s responsibility, often with the tenant’s ID details and photo. Many state police websites or apps allow online submission. It protects both sides. Keep a copy.

steps.title: Rent receipts and HRA
steps.body: Pay rent through bank transfer/UPI and keep **rent receipts** (signed, with landlord name, address, amount, period). Salaried employees claiming **HRA exemption** (available in the old tax regime) usually need rent receipts, and employers typically ask for the **landlord’s PAN when annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh**. Never make fake rent receipts — the tax department can verify.

steps.title: First-week setup
steps.body:
- Change or re-key locks if allowed (agree in writing).
- Update your address: bank, Aadhaar (address update), employer, delivery apps.
- Save numbers: landlord, society office, plumber, electrician, nearest hospital, police station.
- Check smoke and gas safety; know the fire exit.

steps.title: Try this
steps.body: Make an inventory template in your notes app now: Room → Item → Condition → Photo taken (Y/N).

activity.prompt: Put the move-in steps in a sensible order.
items: Sign and keep a copy of the agreement
Pay deposit by bank transfer and get a receipt
Walk through with landlord and record a dated video
Note meter readings and make an inventory
Email photos, inventory and readings to the landlord
Complete police tenant verification as required
Update your address with bank and other services

quiz.q: Why email move-in photos to the landlord?
options: Creates dated proof of the flat’s condition
quiz.why: Emailing move-in photos creates dated proof of the flat's condition, which prevents unfair deductions later. It does not give discounts or Wi-Fi.

options: A safety registration required in many cities
quiz.why: Police tenant verification is a safety registration required in many cities. It is not a tax or an electricity bill, and is not optional everywhere.

quiz.q: Employers usually ask for the landlord’s PAN for HRA when yearly rent exceeds…
quiz.why: Employers usually require the landlord's PAN for HRA when annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh. Below that, it is generally not needed.
Pay rent by bank transfer or UPI and keep receipts, since a traceable payment is proof. Cash without receipts, vouchers or payment through a friend leave no clear record.

sources: Income Tax Department guidance on HRA

lessons.title: Problems, moving out and getting your deposit back

scenes.text: After two years in Ahmedabad, Kavya gives two months’ notice in writing as her agreement requires.
The landlord says he will deduct full repainting, a deep clean and ‘wear and tear’ — almost the entire deposit.
Kavya replies calmly with her move-in video, the agreement clause and quotes for the actual broken items.
They agree on a fair deduction for one broken window latch. Her deposit returns within the agreed 30 days.

steps.title: Wear and tear vs damage
steps.body: **Normal wear and tear** is the natural ageing from ordinary living: slightly faded paint, minor scuffs, loose hinges from use. **Damage** is harm beyond normal use: holes in walls, broken tiles, burnt counters, stained mattresses. Fair deductions usually cover **damage** and **unpaid dues**, not ordinary ageing — but your agreement’s specific clauses (for example, an agreed painting charge) matter.

steps.title: Moving-out steps
steps.body:
1. Give **written notice** (email/WhatsApp + letter) as per notice period.
2. Pay final bills; take final meter readings and photos.
3. Repair what you broke; clean the flat.
4. Do a joint inspection; compare with move-in inventory.
5. Return all keys against a written acknowledgement.
6. Ask for the deposit refund with an itemised list of any deductions, by bank transfer.

steps.title: Handling disputes calmly
steps.body:
- Keep everything **in writing**; be polite and factual.
- Offer evidence: agreement clause, move-in video, receipts, quotes for repair costs.
- Propose a fair compromise.
- If it fails: send a formal letter, then a lawyer’s legal notice. Depending on the state, you may approach the **Rent Controller / Rent Authority** (where applicable) or a **civil court**. Free legal aid is available through **Legal Services Authorities** for eligible people.

steps.title: During the tenancy
steps.body:
- Don’t stop paying rent to ‘punish’ the landlord over repairs — it weakens your position. Write and keep records.
- Landlords generally should give **reasonable notice** before visiting, as per your agreement.
- Don’t sublet without written permission.
- Report any illegal eviction attempt (cutting water/electricity, changing locks) to police and seek legal help.
This is general education, not legal advice.

steps.title: Around the world
steps.body: In England and Wales, for most assured shorthold tenancies, deposits must be placed in a government-approved deposit protection scheme. Many countries have similar rules. In India protections depend on state law and your agreement — which is why documentation is your best friend.

a.text: Moving out, your landlord says: ‘I’m keeping ₹40,000 of your ₹50,000 deposit for painting and general wear.’ Your agreement says only damage beyond normal wear will be deducted.

choices.label: Shout and refuse to return keys
choices.feedback: Withholding keys can put you in the wrong and escalates the dispute.

choices.label: Reply in writing with the clause, move-in video, and ask for an itemised list

b.text: He sends a list: repainting ₹30,000 (walls only faded), broken latch ₹1,000, cleaning ₹2,000.

choices.label: Accept the latch and cleaning, dispute the painting with evidence and suggest a settlement
Accept everything to avoid conflict
choices.feedback: You may lose money you’re fairly owed.

bad.text: The dispute worsens. Return keys against acknowledgement and restart with written, evidence-based communication.

meh.text: Peaceful but costly. Next time, document and negotiate — fairness is not the same as conflict.

good.text: He agrees to deduct ₹3,000. You get ₹47,000 back by bank transfer. Documentation wins.

quiz.q: Which is normal wear and tear?
options: Slightly faded paint after two years
quiz.why: Slightly faded paint after two years is normal wear and tear from ordinary living. A hole in a wall, a broken window or a burnt counter is damage the tenant may pay for.

quiz.q: How should you give notice when moving out?
options: In writing, as per the notice period
quiz.why: Give notice in writing, as per the notice period in the agreement, because written notice is proof. Verbal notice or a message through a neighbour is hard to prove.

quiz.q: If a deposit dispute can’t be settled, a next step can be…
options: Legal notice, then rent authority/court depending on state
quiz.why: If a deposit dispute cannot be settled, send a legal notice and then go to the rent authority or court, depending on the state. Use formal, lawful channels, not shaming or damaging the flat.

quiz.q: Stopping rent because repairs are delayed is…
options: Risky — it can weaken your position; document and communicate instead
quiz.why: Withholding rent over delayed repairs is risky because it can put you in breach and weaken your position. Keep paying, document the problem, send written requests and use lawful remedies.

questions.q: Before paying any money for a flat you should…
options: Visit it and verify the owner
questions.why: Before paying anything, visit the flat and verify that the person is the real owner. Photos and pressure to pay quickly or in cash are typical of rental fraud.

options: Dated and shared with the landlord
questions.why: Dated move-in photos shared with the landlord are proof of the flat's initial condition, which protects your deposit later. Deleting them or taking them after a year defeats the purpose.

questions.q: A rent of ₹12,000 with take-home ₹40,000 is…
questions.why: Rent share = 12,000 ÷ 40,000 = 0.30, which is 30% of take-home pay. That is at the upper end of the usual 25–30% guideline.

options: You can’t leave before it ends without penalty (as agreed)
questions.why: A lock-in period is a minimum commitment: you cannot leave before it ends without the penalty agreed in the contract. It has nothing to do with door locks or deposit refunds.

questions.q: Which is the landlord’s typical responsibility?
questions.why: Structural and major repairs, such as serious seepage, usually fall on the landlord. Tenants normally pay for their own groceries and internet and for damage they cause, like a bulb they broke.

questions.q: Agreements of one year or more generally require…
questions.why: Agreements of one year or more generally need registration under the Registration Act 1908, which is why many are for 11 months. Police approval or a passport is not the requirement.

questions.q: Which document helps claim HRA exemption?
questions.why: Rent receipts are the proof employers require to allow an HRA exemption. Movie tickets, a gas bill or a meter photo do not show rent paid.

options: A model law states may adopt
questions.why: The Model Tenancy Act 2021 is a model law that states may adopt or adapt by enacting their own versions. It is not automatically mandatory, nor limited to shops.

questions.q: Total move-in cash: rent ₹15,000, deposit 2 months, brokerage 1 month, plus first month’s rent. How much?
questions.why: Deposit of 2 months = 2 × 15,000 = 30,000; brokerage 1 month = 15,000; first month's rent = 15,000. Total = 30,000 + 15,000 + 15,000 = ₹60,000.

questions.q: Landlord cuts electricity to force you out mid-tenancy. Best response?
options: Document, write to him, report to police and seek legal help
questions.why: Cutting essential services to force a tenant out is an illegal eviction tactic. Document it, write to the landlord, report to police and seek legal help; retaliating or stopping rent weakens your case.

questions.q: Which clause is most likely to cause a deposit dispute?
options: Refund within 30 days by bank transfer
Itemised deductions for damage beyond normal wear
questions.why: 'Deductions at owner's sole discretion' has no objective limits, so it is the likeliest to cause a dispute. Joint inspection, itemised deductions and a refund deadline give clarity.

questions.q: Strongest evidence package in a deposit dispute?
options: Signed agreement, dated move-in video/inventory, written notice, final readings, key handover acknowledgement
questions.why: The strongest package is documents and dated media: the signed agreement, move-in video or inventory, written notice, final readings and key handover acknowledgement. Memory, posts or opinions carry little weight.

questions.q: A friend in Maharashtra plans an unregistered 11-month leave-and-licence agreement. Best advice?

questions.why: Rules differ by state, and Maharashtra requires leave-and-licence agreements to be registered, with online registration available. A verbal or unregistered agreement leaves the friend with little proof.

lessons.title: Histamine and the H1 receptor

scenes.text: Aarav cleans the attic before Diwali and starts sneezing non-stop, eyes streaming.
His immune system has mistaken dust-mite protein for an enemy.
A small cetirizine tablet calms it down. How?

steps.title: Learning, not medical advice
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or pharmacist. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: The allergic reaction
steps.body: In allergy, **IgE antibodies** sit on **mast cells**. When the allergen (pollen, dust mite, pet dander) binds, mast cells release **histamine** and other mediators. Histamine on **H1 receptors** causes itching, sneezing, runny nose, watery eyes, hives (urticaria), and blood-vessel leakiness.

steps.title: How H1 antihistamines work
steps.body: They are technically **inverse agonists** at H1 receptors — they stabilise the receptor in its inactive state, so histamine cannot switch it on. They work best **before** or early in a reaction. They don't treat the blocked nose of chronic allergy as well as steroid nasal sprays do.

steps.title: Not all histamine receptors
steps.body:
- **H1:** allergy symptoms
- **H2:** stomach acid (blocked by famotidine)
- **H3/H4:** brain and immune cells
So 'antihistamine' in everyday speech means H1 blockers.

activity.prompt: Order the allergic chain.
items: First exposure: body makes IgE to dust-mite protein
IgE coats mast cells
Re-exposure: allergen binds IgE on mast cells
Mast cells release histamine
Histamine activates H1 receptors
Sneezing, itching, watery eyes

options: Before or early in a reaction

lessons.title: Lab: First vs second generation

scenes.text: Tanvi took an old cold tablet with chlorphenamine for hay fever the night before her exam.
She feels foggy and slow in the morning.
A newer antihistamine might have helped without the hangover.

steps.title: Why some cause sleepiness
steps.body: **First-generation** antihistamines (chlorphenamine, diphenhydramine, promethazine, hydroxyzine) are fat-soluble and cross the **blood–brain barrier**, blocking brain H1 receptors that keep us alert. They also block **muscarinic** (anticholinergic) receptors → dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, confusion in older adults.

steps.title: Second generation
steps.body: **Cetirizine**, **levocetirizine** (the active half of cetirizine), **loratadine**, **desloratadine**, **fexofenadine**, **bilastine** cross into the brain much less. Cetirizine can still make some people drowsy; fexofenadine and loratadine least. Usually once daily.

steps.title: Real-world risk
steps.body: Next-day impairment after a first-generation antihistamine can be similar to driving after alcohol. Never mix with alcohol, sleeping pills or opioids.

steps.title: Older adults
steps.body: Strongly anticholinergic first-generation drugs are on lists of 'potentially inappropriate' medicines for older people because of confusion, falls and urinary retention.

lessons.title: Lab: Anaphylaxis — when allergy becomes an emergency

scenes.text: At a birthday party, 15-year-old Dev eats a laddoo containing peanuts.
Within minutes his lips swell, he is wheezing and dizzy.
Antihistamine tablets are not enough. This is anaphylaxis.

steps.title: Recognise it
steps.body: Sudden onset after a trigger (food, insect sting, medicine) with **Airway** (swelling of lips/tongue/throat, hoarse voice), **Breathing** (wheeze, breathlessness) or **Circulation** problems (pale, floppy, fainting, collapse), often with hives.

steps.title: What to do
steps.body:
1. Call **112**.
2. If the person has an **adrenaline (epinephrine) auto-injector**, use it in the outer thigh — adrenaline is the first-line treatment.
3. Lie them flat with legs raised (sit up if breathing is hard; recovery position if unconscious; pregnant women on the left side).
4. A second adrenaline dose may be given after about 5 minutes if no improvement (per device instructions).
5. Antihistamines only help skin symptoms — they do **not** replace adrenaline.

steps.title: Why hospital even after improving
steps.body: Symptoms can return hours later (biphasic reaction), so everyone treated for anaphylaxis needs medical observation.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Relying on tablets instead of adrenaline in anaphylaxis
- Taking sedating antihistamines before driving or exams
- Mixing with alcohol or sleeping pills
- Giving strongly sedating ones to frail elderly people

bad.text: His breathing worsens. Adrenaline and 112 were needed immediately.

end2.text: Risky — always get observation after anaphylaxis.

courses.title: Acidity medicines: antacids, H2 blockers and PPIs
courses.summary: How the stomach makes acid, how antacids neutralise it, how H2 blockers and proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole, pantoprazole) switch it down, the risks of long-term PPI use, and the alarm symptoms that need a doctor.
outcomes: Learners can explain the proton pump and acid secretion
Learners can compare antacids, H2 blockers and PPIs

lessons.title: The stomach's acid factory

scenes.text: Vikram eats a heavy biryani at midnight and lies straight down.
A burning rises behind his breastbone — heartburn.
To understand the medicines, first meet the proton pump.

steps.title: Learning, not medical advice
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or pharmacist. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Parietal cells
steps.body: Stomach **parietal cells** secrete hydrochloric acid using the **H+/K+ ATPase** — the **proton pump**. It is switched on by three signals: **histamine** (via H2 receptors), **gastrin**, and **acetylcholine** (vagus nerve). Stomach pH can reach about 1–2.

steps.title: Why the stomach doesn't digest itself
steps.body: Mucus and bicarbonate layer, tight cell junctions, rapid cell renewal and prostaglandins (which is why NSAIDs harm). **H. pylori** infection and NSAIDs are the two main causes of peptic ulcers.

steps.title: Reflux (GERD)
steps.body: When the lower oesophageal sphincter relaxes, acid flows up → heartburn, sour taste. Triggers: large late meals, lying down soon after eating, obesity, smoking, alcohol, some foods, pregnancy.

activity.prompt: Match each part to its role.
pairs: Proton pump — final step of acid secretion

quiz.q: Two main causes of peptic ulcers:
Heartburn after lying down post-meal is due to…
options: Reflux of acid into the oesophagus

lessons.title: Lab: Antacid, H2 blocker or PPI?

scenes.text: Occasional heartburn after a wedding feast. Night-time acidity for weeks. A diagnosed ulcer.
Each calls for a different kind of medicine.

steps.title: Antacids
steps.body: Bases (magnesium hydroxide, aluminium hydroxide, calcium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate) that **neutralise** acid already in the stomach. Fast (minutes), short-lived. Magnesium can loosen stools; aluminium can constipate; sodium bicarbonate adds salt. Antacids can **block absorption** of some drugs (e.g. some antibiotics, iron, levothyroxine) — space them apart.

steps.title: H2 blockers
steps.body: **Famotidine** blocks histamine at H2 receptors on parietal cells → less acid for several hours. (Ranitidine was withdrawn in many countries in 2020 over NDMA impurity concerns.)

steps.title: PPIs
steps.body: **Omeprazole, pantoprazole, esomeprazole, rabeprazole, lansoprazole** irreversibly block the proton pump itself — the most powerful acid reduction. They are **prodrugs** activated in acid, so they work best taken **before a meal** (commonly 30–60 min before breakfast). Full effect takes a few days. Used for GERD, ulcers, H. pylori eradication (with antibiotics) and protecting high-risk NSAID users.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Taking PPIs after meals instead of before
- Staying on PPIs for years without a review
- Calling chest pain 'gas'
- Taking antacids together with thyroid tablets, iron or some antibiotics

lessons.title: Lab: Long-term PPIs and alarm symptoms

scenes.text: Sunita, 55, has taken pantoprazole every morning for 5 years after a short course once.
She now has tingling feet and low B12.
Her doctor reviews whether she still needs it.

steps.title: Possible long-term PPI effects
steps.body: Associated (not all proven causal) with: **vitamin B12 deficiency**, **low magnesium**, possibly reduced calcium absorption and fracture risk, **C. difficile** and other gut infections, and rarely kidney inflammation (interstitial nephritis). Many people take PPIs longer than needed — regular review is good practice.

steps.title: Rebound
steps.body: Stopping suddenly after long use can cause **rebound acid hypersecretion** for a few weeks. Doctors may step down gradually.

steps.title: Alarm symptoms → doctor (don't just self-treat)
steps.body:
- Difficulty or pain swallowing
- Unintended weight loss
- Vomiting blood or black stools
- Persistent vomiting
- Anaemia
- New symptoms over about 55, or family history of stomach cancer
- Chest pain with sweating/breathlessness → could be the **heart**: call 112

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Taking PPIs after meals instead of before
- Staying on PPIs for years without a review
- Calling chest pain 'gas'
- Taking antacids together with thyroid tablets, iron or some antibiotics

courses.title: Diarrhoea: ORS, zinc, loperamide and danger signs
courses.summary: Why oral rehydration solution is one of medicine's greatest inventions, the science of sodium–glucose co-transport, zinc for children, how loperamide works and when it must not be used, and the signs of dangerous dehydration.
outcomes: Learners can explain how ORS works

lessons.title: Lab: The science of ORS

scenes.text: After street food in June heat, Ravi has watery diarrhoea six times.
He drinks a sugary cola. His friend hands him an ORS sachet instead.
Why is ORS better than cola or plain water?

steps.title: Learning, not medical advice
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or pharmacist. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Sodium–glucose co-transport
steps.body: In most infectious diarrhoea, the gut still has a working transporter (**SGLT1**) that moves **sodium and glucose together** into intestinal cells; water follows by osmosis. ORS gives sodium and glucose in the right ratio so the gut absorbs water even while diarrhoea continues.

steps.title: Low-osmolarity ORS
steps.body: WHO/UNICEF **reduced-osmolarity ORS** (total osmolarity **245 mOsm/L**) has less sodium and glucose than the older formula and reduces stool output and vomiting. ORS has saved millions of lives since the 1970s.

steps.title: Why not cola or juice?
steps.body: Too much sugar and too little sodium → high osmolarity that can **pull water into the gut** and worsen diarrhoea. Plain water alone doesn't replace salts.

steps.title: Prepare correctly
steps.body: Dissolve one sachet in the exact volume of clean (boiled and cooled) water printed on the pack — usually 1 litre. Too concentrated is dangerous; too dilute is less effective. Use within 24 hours.

activity.prompt: Order the ORS preparation steps.
items: Wash hands with soap
Boil water and let it cool
Measure the exact volume printed on the sachet
Empty the whole sachet into the water
Stir until fully dissolved
Give small frequent sips; discard after 24 hours

quiz.q: ORS works because sodium and glucose are absorbed together via…

options: Too much sugar, too little sodium

quiz.q: A sachet meant for 1 L dissolved in 250 mL would be…

lessons.title: Lab: Dehydration danger signs in children

scenes.text: Meher, 14 months, has had diarrhoea for a day and is now very sleepy.
Her eyes look sunken and a pinched skin fold goes back slowly.
These are signs of severe dehydration.

steps.title: Severe dehydration (urgent care, 112)
steps.body:
- Lethargic or unconscious
- Sunken eyes
- Unable to drink or drinks poorly
- Skin pinch goes back **very slowly**
- Very little or no urine; no tears
Also urgent: blood in stool, high fever, repeated vomiting, convulsions, age under 6 months with diarrhoea.

steps.title: Home care for mild cases (with medical advice)
steps.body: Continue breastfeeding and normal food, give ORS after each loose stool, and **zinc** for children as recommended by WHO and India's national programmes (a health worker advises the amount and duration). Zinc shortens diarrhoea and reduces recurrence.

steps.title: India
steps.body: Diarrhoea remains a major cause of death in young children. Public campaigns (e.g. the intensified diarrhoea control fortnight) promote 'ORS + zinc'. Rotavirus vaccine is part of India's Universal Immunization Programme.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Mixing ORS in too little water
- Using cola or juice instead of ORS
- Using loperamide for bloody diarrhoea or in young children
- Stopping breastfeeding or food during diarrhoea

lessons.title: Lab: Loperamide — when yes, when absolutely not

scenes.text: Kiran has mild traveller's diarrhoea and a 6-hour bus ride.
A pharmacist mentions loperamide for short-term relief in adults.
But for her friend with bloody diarrhoea and fever, it's a different story.

steps.title: Mechanism
steps.body: **Loperamide** is an opioid that acts on **μ-opioid receptors in the gut wall**, slowing movement (peristalsis) and increasing fluid absorption. At normal doses it barely enters the brain because a pump (**P-glycoprotein**) pushes it out.

steps.title: Avoid when
steps.body:
- **Blood in the stool** or high fever (possible dysentery — slowing the gut can worsen invasive infections)
- Suspected **C. difficile** colitis (e.g. after antibiotics)
- **Young children** (not for children under the label age)
- Abdominal swelling, constipation, or ulcerative colitis flare
It does NOT replace ORS.

steps.title: Overdose
steps.body: Very high doses (misused by some people) can cause dangerous **heart rhythm problems** (QT prolongation, arrhythmias) and death. Stay within the label.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Mixing ORS in too little water
- Using cola or juice instead of ORS
- Using loperamide for bloody diarrhoea or in young children
- Stopping breastfeeding or food during diarrhoea

courses.summary: Laxative types and their risks, how anti-sickness medicines differ, why 'gas' is often blamed wrongly, and common gut myths in Indian households.

lessons.title: Laxatives: types and traps

scenes.text: Mrs Kapoor has taken a herbal 'churan' laxative every night for 10 years.
Her doctor finds it contains senna, a stimulant laxative, and her potassium is low.

steps.title: Learning, not medical advice
steps.body: This is for learning, not medical advice. For your own health, talk to a doctor or pharmacist. In an emergency call 112.

steps.title: Types
steps.body:
- **Bulk-forming** (psyllium/isabgol): absorbs water, adds bulk — needs plenty of fluid
- **Osmotic** (lactulose, polyethylene glycol, magnesium salts): draw water into the bowel
- **Stimulant** (senna, bisacodyl): stimulate gut nerves/muscle — cramps; long-term heavy use can cause low potassium
- **Softeners** (docusate) and **suppositories** (glycerin)

steps.title: First steps
steps.body: Fibre (fruit, vegetables, whole grains, pulses), 6–8 glasses of fluid as appropriate, movement, not ignoring the urge, and reviewing medicines that constipate (iron, opioids, some antacids, anticholinergics).

steps.title: Red flags
steps.body: Blood in stool, unexplained weight loss, a new persistent change in bowel habit over ~50, anaemia, severe pain/vomiting with no stool or gas (possible obstruction → urgent).

life-medicines-antibiotics-vaccines.title: Antibiotics, resistance & vaccines
life-medicines-antibiotics-vaccines.description: How antibiotics kill bacteria, why they do nothing for viral fever, how antimicrobial resistance develops, why courses matter, how vaccines train immunity, and how India's Universal Immunization Programme works. General education, not medical advice.

courses.title: How antibiotics work
courses.summary: Bacteria vs viruses, the main antibiotic targets (cell wall, protein synthesis, DNA, folate), bactericidal vs bacteriostatic, spectrum, common side effects and allergies.
outcomes: Learners can distinguish bacteria from viruses
Learners can match antibiotic classes to targets
